title: The EU–Brazil Digital Partnership: what's actually in it, and why it matters
subtitle: On 12 June 2026, Brussels and Brasília drew a digital bridge across the Atlantic, a Digital Partnership built on a January adequacy decision that quietly created the world's largest free-data-flow zone, covering 670 million people. Here's what's actually in it, and why it matters to Regen Studio, with one foot in EU regulation and one in Brazil.
featuredImageAlt: A faceted, low-poly bridge of colourful triangular polygons spanning between the EU and Brazilian flags' colours, illustrating the EU–Brazil Digital Partnership and the free flow of data across the Atlantic
excerpt: On 12 June 2026 the EU and Brazil signed a Digital Partnership in Brasília, easy to file under 'diplomatic communiqué' and move on. But underneath the framing sit concrete workstreams on data, identity, chips and connectivity, built on a January 2026 adequacy decision that created the world's largest free-data-flow zone, covering 670 million people. Here's what was actually signed, the piece most coverage buried, and why it's directly relevant to the unglamorous engineering of trustworthy cross-border digital systems.
